basis: Microcephaly, epilepsy and diabetes define the syndrome; each occurs in 6/6 reported patients.
EBV-driven B-cell lymphoproliferation chiefly affects lungs; CNS infiltration occurs in ~30-40% overall; skin involvement ~30-40% omitted by cap; grade-specific rates uncertain.
DiGeorge-2 deletion phenotype includes developmental disability, hypoparathyroidism and thymic deficiency; congenital cardiac defects are a major syndromic feature.
Hormone resistance and Albright osteodystrophy define disease; intellectual disability and cataracts each 30-79%; dental enamel defects 30-79% omitted by cap.
Endocrine dysfunction, neurodegeneration and alopecia define disease; sensorineural hearing loss 80-99% in HPO; osteopenia 80-99% omitted by cap.
Moniezia tapeworms occupy the intestine; supplied definition describes infection in ruminants.
Cutis laxa, skeletal abnormalities and gingival overgrowth define syndrome; prolonged bleeding time 3/3 supports haemostatic dysfunction; cognitive impairment 30-79% omitted by cap.
Inherited coagulation disorder; supplied definition explicitly describes venous thrombosis. Organ-specific embolic complications are not added.
Congenital unilateral absence of forearm bones and hand structures.
Urethral disorder; the urinary tract is covered by the renal axis. Infection is not inherent.
Umbrella for infantile multisystem autoimmunity; no particular damaged organ is established as common across its heterogeneous subtypes.
Benign neoplasm arising from cutaneous sweat glands.
X-linked Dyggve-Melchior-Clausen phenotype combines spondyloepimetaphyseal skeletal dysplasia and intellectual disability.
Intestinal tapeworm infection; gastrointestinal occupation defines its site even when asymptomatic. Anaemia is not established as common.
Inherited proximal tubular dysfunction with low-molecular-weight proteinuria and nephrocalcinosis, both reported in all assessed patients.
Chondrodysplasia defines skeletal disease; steroid sulfatase deficiency is an inborn metabolic defect causing ichthyosis in most affected males.
CRYAA-related cataract is a lens disorder; accompanying abnormalities remain within the ocular axis.
Persistent conjunctival inflammation; the umbrella includes multiple causes and does not establish an infectious or immune-mediated mechanism throughout.
Urinary tract developmental malformations are established by the listed subtypes and Q60-Q64 cross-reference.
Defined acid-base disorder; no particular causal organ disorder or lasting secondary organ injury is inherent.
Umbrella for inborn glycolytic metabolic disorders; blood, muscle and nerve damage vary by subtype and are not shared throughout.
Sclerosing bone dysplasia, ichthyosis and endocrine ovarian failure are the defining triad; each has very frequent HPO support.
Developmental disability defines syndrome; optic hypoplasia/atrophy 80-99%, visual impairment 6/9, hydronephrosis and metatarsus adductus each 30-79%.
Cerebellar/brainstem malformation defines disease; oculomotor apraxia is central. Hepatic fibrosis 2/7 is borderline; damaging retinal and renal disease not clearly >=30%.
Benign familial megalencephaly/macrocephaly is a brain-growth phenotype; skull shape alone does not establish a separate skeletal disorder.
